instruction: Calculate how much more was spent on Gas & Electric in 2019 compared to 2020. Put the difference (2019 total minus 2020 total) in cell B33.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to create two column charts for 2019 and 2020 monthly costs. It understood the data structure and SUM formulas but struggled with multi-range selection in the chart wizard. Created one incomplete chart for 2019 but never created the second chart. Ran out of 50 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Calc cells, understand data layout, use formulas (SUM), open Insert menu, interact with chart wizard dialog
metadata.failure_analysis: Failed to correctly select non-contiguous data ranges (months + totals) for chart creation. Spent excessive turns trying different selection methods. Only created one chart with incorrect data, never started second chart.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a subtraction formula comparing two yearly totals. Model demonstrated it can understand the two-table layout and navigate between them.
metadata.explanation: Task asks model to compute difference between 2019 Gas & Electric total (B15=515) and 2020 total (B32=460), placing result 55 in B33. Evaluator checks B33 for exact value 55.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads cell B33 from sheet 0 of the target xlsx file using openpyxl with data_only=True, matching the instruction requirement.
Metric correctly handles the expected parameter as the rules dict directly (expected.get('expected_value')), consistent with the get_rule framework for type='rule'.
Expected value of 55 is semantically correct: 2019 Gas & Electric total (B15=515) minus 2020 total (B32=460) = 55, as documented in metadata.
Postconfig properly activates the LibreOffice Calc window and saves the file (Ctrl+S) before reading, ensuring formula results are cached for data_only=True parsing.
Complete instruction coverage: the single requirement (difference value in B33) is fully verified by the evaluator.
Tolerance of 0.01 is appropriate for an integer subtraction result, allowing for minor floating-point representation differences.
